question: Can any symmetric positive-definite passive linear stiffness matrix with the same stiffness trace achieve at least 1.5 times the direction-neutral rigid-translation magnetic-error performance of the declared uncoupled directional control on the published SIMSOPT NCSX modular-coil geometry?
assumptions: The NCSX coil coefficients, currents, symmetry expansion, and plasma-boundary coefficients follow the declared public SIMSOPT files at the bound upstream commit.
Each of the 18 physical modular coils has three rigid local translation degrees of freedom; bending, rotation, casing strain, joints, preload, fatigue, and the surrounding structure are excluded.

For H = S^T S, minimizing tr(H K^-2) over every symmetric positive-definite K with fixed trace has the global closed-form solution in which K shares H's eigenvectors and its eigenvalues are proportional to the cube roots of H's eigenvalues.
The full 54 by 54 stiffness matrix is an intentionally generous mathematical relaxation containing nonlocal and cross-direction coupling; it is not claimed to be mechanically realizable.
The complete orthogonal translation-load basis is direction-neutral and is not a probability distribution or reactor load spectrum.

The 1.5 reduction target and numerical limits are inherited from CASE-004. Passing would justify only a realizable-topology search; failure means that no candidate inside this relaxed passive linear model can reach that target on the discretized reference geometry.

requirements.statement: The fine-grid global passive linear ceiling is at least 1.5 times the declared uncoupled directional control.
The ideal full-matrix realization has worst compliance no more than twice the unit isotropic support.
The ideal full-matrix realization has stiffness condition number no greater than 10.
The worst reference-grid linear-versus-exact displaced-geometry error is no more than 10 percent.
The ceiling changes by no more than 15 percent from the reference to fine discretization.
The fine-grid magnetic sensitivity changes by no more than 2 percent when the central-difference step is halved.
